title: METRICS MONITORING (DATADOG)
subtitle: Millions of data points per second arrive, and alerts must fire within a minute.
footer: DDIA: Ch 3 LSM, compression · Ch 11 stream alerting   ·   Similar: Top-K videos · Ad click aggregator · Web crawler · Fitness tracking

items: Buffer the write firehose through Kafka into a time-series database built for appends and compression.
Downsample old data and move it to cheap storage; dashboards read rollups.
Evaluate alert rules on the stream itself instead of polling the database.

Naive: one Postgres row per datapoint with a B-tree index. It falls over around ~50k inserts/sec.

items: Buffer through Kafka into a time-series DB: append-only LSM writes, series-by-time blocks, delta-of-delta + XOR compression.
Queries hit recent blocks; older data is downsampled (1s → 1m → 1h) and tiered to S3. Dashboards use rollups.
Alerts are evaluated on the stream (Flink windows over Kafka), not by polling the TSDB with thousands of queries.
Time-ordered appends suit LSM; compression gives ~10×; queries are range scans per series.
A user_id tag explodes series count. Cap or reject high-cardinality labels.
Event-time windows with watermarks; allowed lateness for corrections.
Require N consecutive windows; dedupe and group in the alert manager.
Row-per-point in Postgres, and alerting by polling queries.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
